ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines AB and CD intersect at O, OA bisects $\angle COE$, and $\angle COE \colon \angle BOE = 2 \colon 5$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle EOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle COE : \angle BOE = 2 : 5$,\\
let $\angle COE = 2x$, then $\angle BOE = 5x$,\\
Since OA bisects $\angle COE$,\\
thus $\angle AOE = \angle COA = \angle BOD = x$,\\
thus $\angle DOE = 4x$,\\
Since $\angle COE + \angle DOE = 180^\circ$,\\
thus $2x + 4x = 180^\circ$,\\
thus $x = 30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle DOE = 4x = \boxed{120^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines AB and CD intersect at O, OA bisects $\angle COE$, and $\angle COE : \angle BOE = 2 : 5$. What is the degree measure of $\angle EOD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle COE : \angle BOE = 2 : 5$,\\ let $\angle COE = 2x$, then $\angle BOE = 5x$,\\ Since OA bisects $\angle COE$,\\ thus $\angle AOE = \angle COA = \angle BOD = x$,\\ thus $\angle DOE = 4x$,\\ Since $\angle COE + \angle DOE = 180^\circ$,\\ thus $2x + 4x = 180^\circ$,\\ thus $x = 30^\circ$,\\ thus $\angle DOE = 4x = \boxed{120^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, line AB passes horizontally through O, with A on the left and B on the right, so OA and OB are opposite rays; line CD passes obliquely through O, with C at the lower left and D at the upper right, so OC and OD are opposite rays; ray OE points from O toward the upper left, located in the upper region of the figure. Reasoning: It is known that OA bisects ∠COE, and ∠COE : ∠BOE = 2 : 5. Let ∠COE = y. Then because OA bisects ∠COE, ∠AOE = y/2. Also because OA and OB are opposite rays, ∠AOE and ∠BOE form a pair of adjacent supplementary angles, so ∠BOE = 180° - y/2. From the ratio y : (180° - y/2) = 2 : 5, we get 5y = 2(180° - y/2) = 360° - y, therefore 6y = 360°, y = 60°. Finally, because OC and OD are opposite rays, ∠COE and ∠EOD form adjacent supplementary angles, so ∠EOD = 180° - 60° = 120°.
